decisions.reason: As an environmental sensor module built directly on the firm's modular electronics, firmware, and API stack, it remains close to existing knowledge and therefore worth keeping despite some risk of portfolio simplification or hardware refresh.
Because it is a core measurement module and already a successor generation of an established product, the firm has strong prior knowledge and clear absorptive capacity to support and improve it.
The CAN bus interface stays close to the firm's embedded and automation customer base, so it is still a good fit for the platform even if niche demand could eventually limit its priority.
A carbon dioxide sensor module fits squarely within the firm's sensing capabilities and customer applications, giving the firm good scope to learn from use cases and refine it further.

The touch panel accessory is more peripheral to the firm's core sensing, control, and communication competencies, so under an absorptive-capacity logic its resources are better shifted to more knowledge-adjacent modules and software development.
